acceptanceCriteria: The literal mask recognises /.../, %r{...} and %r(...) regex literals in an operand position, and does not treat a quote inside them as opening a string
Fixture: `x =~ /'/` followed by `Foo::Bar.call` still extracts Foo::Bar; division `a / b` is unaffected
The RUBY-AFFECTED-V0-043 limit is removed or narrowed, with a test traced to it
body: The Ruby affected scanner masks string literals before it extracts constants. It does not recognise regex literals, so a quote inside one, such as `x =~ /'/`, opens a string that runs to the next quote. Constants referenced inside that span are hidden, which can drop a dependency edge and under-select tests. This is recorded as a limit in RUBY-AFFECTED-V0-043 (batch-affected-appmap-ruby, #1395). It needs the regex-vs-division ambiguity handled the way Ruby's lexer does: after an operator or keyword, `/` starts a regex.

title: Ruby affected literal mask: a quote inside a regex literal (/'/) opens a string and hides later constants
